title: Consolidation of power in two authoritarian states
stem: Paper 2 essay practice. Answer with reference to two authoritarian states, each chosen from a different region where the question requires it. Plan for about 45 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare and contrast the methods used by two authoritarian leaders to consolidate their power.
markscheme: Introduction: names two states (e.g. Hitler's Germany and Stalin's USSR), defines consolidation and states a comparative thesis
Structure is thematic and comparative (e.g. legal methods, terror, propaganda, removal of rivals), not two separate narratives
Legal/constitutional methods: Enabling Act and Gleichschaltung (1933) versus Stalin's use of party posts and congress votes as General Secretary
Removal of rivals: Night of the Long Knives (1934) versus defeat of Trotsky, Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin (1924–29), later show trials
Terror: Gestapo, SS and camps versus NKVD, Great Terror (1936–38) and Gulag; difference in scale and timing
Propaganda and cult of personality: Goebbels and the Führer myth versus Stalin's cult and rewriting of history
Economic policy as a tool: rearmament and falling unemployment versus Five-Year Plans and collectivisation
Role of the army and elites: Hitler's need for army and business support versus Stalin's control through the party and purging the Red Army
Historiography used to support analysis (e.g. Kershaw 'working towards the Führer'; Conquest versus Getty on the terror)
Conclusion: reasoned judgement on the most significant similarities and differences
parts.notes: Real Paper 2 essays are marked out of 15 using markbands; this practice version uses a 10-point checklist. Top answers keep a comparative focus in every paragraph.
